facts.fact: Asha's room is the last door at the end of the south passage, shut six years; Janu holds the key on a cord and could not enter it herself. Contents: a camphor-wood chest with a green brass hasp, a cot, a stool, and a leather cap on a peg.
facts.why: needed because Janu asks Devan to clear Asha's chest and he must find the notes there.

facts.fact: Asha's slate, with recruits' names and mothers' villages in faded chalk (matches F063), lies on top of the chest; the name Unni is on it, and Unni now holds the gate.
facts.why: needed because a concrete, personal object grounds the clearing scene and echoes F063.

facts.fact: Asha's notes (forty or fifty, tied in red thread) are each signed with a drawn parrot of five strokes with a whole beak; she drew the west-stair newel 'mended' because she thought a broken beak insulted the bird.
facts.why: needed because the outline requires notes signed with a drawn parrot and sets up the reader's link to Neela's reaction at the newel.

facts.fact: Asha's first forged token is a split-ash tally stick wrapped in oilcloth with the red thread, bearing council wax with the dot-and-split mark matching Devan's beeswax impression of Bhaskaran's tally (F091). A note with it says: 'First one. Not yet. Need a second to be sure. Tell nobody at the gate.'
facts.why: needed because the outline requires the first forged token and a wax match to the new tokens, and the six-year gap implies one of the same three seal boxes.

facts.fact: Devan did not know Asha had kept the first token; he had assumed it was taken by whoever killed her.
facts.why: needed so the discovery is a real reveal.

facts.fact: Asha was four years younger than Devan; Neela laughs at her note about Thursday sparring, where she 'took both points'.
facts.why: needed for the disclosure scene (Asha was 22 at death and Devan 32 now fits four years apart) and for the laugh beat.

facts.fact: Devan's last found note of Asha's reads: 'If you're reading this, I was right, and it's ugly. Say it anyway. The truth protects whoever finds it.' He withholds it from Neela.
facts.why: needed because the outline ends the chapter on Asha's line in his hand.

facts.fact: The palace rider who takes the fort's post down is Sudhi (matches F072), who brings the royal post every ninth day.
facts.why: needed for the Muthu letter scene.

facts.fact: Muthu hands Sudhi a letter sealed in plain grey wax with no mark, and says it is to his mother in Kodiyur; he pauses a half-breath before laughing. Devan believes him.
facts.why: needed because the outline requires the letter handoff and Devan's belief; the pause plants clue C16.
